app.tour.alerts.text.text: {alerts} counts what's new: likes, comments, friend requests and news from your device. {settings} has your profile, password and language, and {show} to see this again.
app.tour.alerts.text.note: The first-run tour: a card over the dimmed app, one step at a time, each with a small moving drawing of the controls it talks about; shown once by itself after signing in and again from Settings' Show the tour. Text of the last step. {alerts} and {settings} are the sections' names (app.shell.section_alerts, app.shell.section_settings); Alerts shows the number of new alerts on its tab, and also says when the device needs attention (an update, a disk). {show} is the button in Settings › Getting started that shows this tour again (app.tour.show). All in bold.

app.tour.alerts.title.note: The first-run tour: a card over the dimmed app, one step at a time, each with a small moving drawing of the controls it talks about; shown once by itself after signing in and again from Settings' Show the tour. Title of the last step, about the Alerts and Settings sections: use the same words as their names (app.shell.section_alerts, app.shell.section_settings).

app.tour.art.caption.note: The first-run tour's moving drawings of the app (never a real person or photo): the caption typed for a new post with two photos.

app.tour.art.collection.note: The first-run tour's moving drawings of the app (never a real person or photo): the name typed for a new collection of photos.

app.tour.art.comment.note: The first-run tour's moving drawings of the app (never a real person or photo): a short comment typed under a friend's photo in Social.

app.tour.art.friend.note: The first-run tour's moving drawings of the app (never a real person or photo): the made-up first name of a friend (a face named in People, the author of a post, the friend added in Friends). A short first name common in your language, for anyone, different from app.tour.art.person.

app.tour.art.person.note: The first-run tour's moving drawings of the app (never a real person or photo): the made-up first name of the person using the app (and of a face in People). A short first name common in your language, for anyone.

app.tour.art.thing.note: The first-run tour's moving drawings of the app (never a real person or photo): a thing the device recognises in photos, typed into the drawing of the search and picked as a chip. Not translated: the device's image tagging names things in English, so the real search would find this word in every language.

app.tour.backup.text.text: This phone copies its photos and videos to your device by itself. Under {sync} you choose what it sends, and {wifi} keeps it off mobile data.
app.tour.backup.text.note: The first-run tour: a card over the dimmed app, one step at a time, each with a small moving drawing of the controls it talks about; shown once by itself after signing in and again from Settings' Show the tour. Text of the step about the photo backup, shown over Settings. {sync} is the heading of Settings' section with the backup's options (app.settings.sync.title) and {wifi} its first switch (app.settings.sync.wifi_only): while it is on, nothing is sent over mobile data. Both in bold.

app.tour.backup.title.note: The first-run tour: a card over the dimmed app, one step at a time, each with a small moving drawing of the controls it talks about; shown once by itself after signing in and again from Settings' Show the tour. Title of the step about this phone copying its own photos and videos to the device (the photo backup).

app.tour.collections.text.text: Select photos and choose {add}, then {new}, to keep them together, like a trip. The button next to the search lists your collections: open one to rename, share or delete it.
app.tour.collections.text.note: The first-run tour: a card over the dimmed app, one step at a time, each with a small moving drawing of the controls it talks about; shown once by itself after signing in and again from Settings' Show the tour. Text of the step about Collections (never albums) on a phone held upright, where the list of collections opens with a button beside the search field at the top of Images. {add} is the selection bar's button (app.shell.add_to_collection) and {new} the first choice it offers (app.photos.collections.new_item), both in bold. An open collection can be renamed, shared as a gallery (a page anyone with its link can see) or deleted; deleting a collection keeps its photos.

app.tour.collections.text_wide.text: Select photos in Images and choose {add}, then {new}, to keep them together, like a trip. Open a collection here to rename it, share it as a gallery or delete it.
app.tour.collections.text_wide.note: The first-run tour: a card over the dimmed app, one step at a time, each with a small moving drawing of the controls it talks about; shown once by itself after signing in and again from Settings' Show the tour. As app.tour.collections.text, on a wide screen (a phone on its side, a tablet), where Collections is an item of the menu at the left and is open behind the card. Images is the photo section (app.shell.section_images).

app.tour.collections.title.note: The first-run tour: a card over the dimmed app, one step at a time, each with a small moving drawing of the controls it talks about; shown once by itself after signing in and again from Settings' Show the tour. Title of the step about Collections (our word for groups of photos, never albums).

app.tour.dates.text.text: Photos are grouped by month, newest first. Drag your finger down the right edge of the photos to jump to any month: the date shows as you go.
app.tour.dates.text.note: The first-run tour: a card over the dimmed app, one step at a time, each with a small moving drawing of the controls it talks about; shown once by itself after signing in and again from Settings' Show the tour. Text of the step about the date scrubber in Images: a thin strip along the right edge of the photos; dragging a finger down it shows the month under the finger in a bubble, and letting go jumps there.

app.tour.dates.title.note: The first-run tour: a card over the dimmed app, one step at a time, each with a small moving drawing of the controls it talks about; shown once by itself after signing in and again from Settings' Show the tour. Title of the step about jumping to a month in Images by dragging along the right edge of the photos.

app.tour.files.text.text: The button beside the folder's path switches between {list}, {grid} and {storage}, which shows what takes up space. Under {sort}, pick an order, and pick it again to reverse it.
app.tour.files.text.note: The first-run tour: a card over the dimmed app, one step at a time, each with a small moving drawing of the controls it talks about; shown once by itself after signing in and again from Settings' Show the tour. Text of the step about Files' views and sorting. The button at the right of the field with the open folder's path opens a menu: {list}, {grid} and {storage} are its three views (app.files.view_list, .view_grid, .view_storage; Storage lists what takes the most room in the folder), and {sort} its heading over the orders (app.files.sort_by: name, size, date created, date modified). All in bold.

app.tour.files.title.note: The first-run tour: a card over the dimmed app, one step at a time, each with a small moving drawing of the controls it talks about; shown once by itself after signing in and again from Settings' Show the tour. Title of the first step about Files: its three views and sorting.

app.tour.friends.text.text: The two-people button at the top opens Friends: share your address there, or type a friend's device name under {add} and tap {send}. A request to you waits under {waiting}: tap {accept}.
app.tour.friends.text.note: The first-run tour: a card over the dimmed app, one step at a time, each with a small moving drawing of the controls it talks about; shown once by itself after signing in and again from Settings' Show the tour. Text of the step about Friends on a phone held upright, where Friends (app.shell.section_friends) opens with the button showing two people at the top of Social. Its top line is this device's own address, with Copy and Share buttons. {add} is the heading over the field for a friend's device name (app.social.friends.add_heading) and {send} its button (common.send). {waiting} is the heading of the requests waiting for an answer (app.social.friends.waiting_answer) and {accept} their button (common.accept). All in bold.

app.tour.friends.text_wide.text: Share your address so friends can add you, or type their device's name under {add} and tap {send}. A request to you waits under {waiting}: tap {accept}.
app.tour.friends.text_wide.note: The first-run tour: a card over the dimmed app, one step at a time, each with a small moving drawing of the controls it talks about; shown once by itself after signing in and again from Settings' Show the tour. As app.tour.friends.text, on a wide screen (a phone on its side, a tablet), where Friends is an item of the menu at the left and is open behind the card.

app.tour.friends.title.note: The first-run tour: a card over the dimmed app, one step at a time, each with a small moving drawing of the controls it talks about; shown once by itself after signing in and again from Settings' Show the tour. Title of the step about the Friends screen.

app.tour.people.text.text: The button next to the search opens People: tap a face to see every photo of that person, or {name} to name them. Two faces of one person? Press and hold one, tap the other and choose {merge}.
app.tour.people.text.note: The first-run tour: a card over the dimmed app, one step at a time, each with a small moving drawing of the controls it talks about; shown once by itself after signing in and again from Settings' Show the tour. Text of the step about People on a phone held upright, where People (app.shell.section_people) opens with a button beside the search field at the top of Images. {name} is the line under a face without a name (app.photos.people.add_name) and {merge} the button that makes several faces one person (app.photos.people.merge), both in bold. A long press selects a face; once one is selected a tap selects another.

app.tour.people.text_wide.text: Tap a face to see every photo of that person, or {name} to name them. Two faces of one person? Press and hold one, tap the other and choose {merge}.
app.tour.people.text_wide.note: The first-run tour: a card over the dimmed app, one step at a time, each with a small moving drawing of the controls it talks about; shown once by itself after signing in and again from Settings' Show the tour. As app.tour.people.text, on a wide screen (a phone on its side, a tablet), where People is an item of the menu at the left and is open behind the card.

app.tour.people.title.note: The first-run tour: a card over the dimmed app, one step at a time, each with a small moving drawing of the controls it talks about; shown once by itself after signing in and again from Settings' Show the tour. Title of the step about People (shown only while face recognition is on): the faces the device found in the photos.

app.tour.post.text.text: Tap +, pick photos or videos from {phone} (this phone) or {synced} (already on your device), write a caption and tap {publish}. It goes from your device to your friends' devices.
app.tour.post.text.note: The first-run tour: a card over the dimmed app, one step at a time, each with a small moving drawing of the controls it talks about; shown once by itself after signing in and again from Settings' Show the tour. Text of the step about publishing a post. + is the round plus button at the top of Social (on a wide screen, the top bar's + New post); keep the + as it is. {phone} and {synced} are the two halves of the switch at the top of the New Post screen (app.social.compose.source_phone, app.social.compose.source_synced) and {publish} its button (app.social.compose.publish), all in bold. A post needs a caption. Posts travel straight from one device to the others, with no cloud in between.

app.tour.post.title.note: The first-run tour: a card over the dimmed app, one step at a time, each with a small moving drawing of the controls it talks about; shown once by itself after signing in and again from Settings' Show the tour. Title of the step that shows how to publish a post in Social.

app.tour.progress.note: The first-run tour: a card over the dimmed app, one step at a time, each with a small moving drawing of the controls it talks about; shown once by itself after signing in and again from Settings' Show the tour. Line at the top left of the card. {step} is the step shown, {total} how many there are (from 13 to 15: People shows only while face recognition is on, and the step about users only to the device's owner). Also read out by screen readers.

app.tour.search.text.text: Type a thing or a place to find photos, or part of a file's name to find it in Files. Each pick for photos shows as a chip; tap its × to remove it.
app.tour.search.text.note: The first-run tour: a card over the dimmed app, one step at a time, each with a small moving drawing of the controls it talks about; shown once by itself after signing in and again from Settings' Show the tour. Text of the step about the search field at the top of Images, while face recognition is off. It suggests the things and places the device recognised in the photos (a beach, a dog, a city), and the files and folders whose name matches. A thing picked shows as a chip (a small rounded label with an × that removes it). Files is the files section (app.shell.section_files).

app.tour.search.text_faces.text: Type a thing, a place or someone's name to find photos, or part of a file's name to find it in Files. Each pick for photos shows as a chip; tap its × to remove it.
app.tour.search.text_faces.note: The first-run tour: a card over the dimmed app, one step at a time, each with a small moving drawing of the controls it talks about; shown once by itself after signing in and again from Settings' Show the tour. As app.tour.search.text, while face recognition is on: the search also suggests the people who were given a name in People.

app.tour.search.title.note: The first-run tour: a card over the dimmed app, one step at a time, each with a small moving drawing of the controls it talks about; shown once by itself after signing in and again from Settings' Show the tour. Title of the step about the search field at the top of Images.

app.tour.select.text.text: Press and hold a photo, then drag across others to select them too. Then choose {share}, {download}, {add} or {delete} in the bar at the bottom.
app.tour.select.text.note: The first-run tour: a card over the dimmed app, one step at a time, each with a small moving drawing of the controls it talks about; shown once by itself after signing in and again from Settings' Show the tour. Text of the step about selecting photos in Images: a long press selects a photo, and moving the finger on from it selects the photos it passes over. The bar that then shows at the bottom has these buttons, among others: {share} (common.share), {download} (common.download), {add} (app.shell.add_to_collection) and {delete} (common.delete), in bold.

app.tour.select.title.note: The first-run tour: a card over the dimmed app, one step at a time, each with a small moving drawing of the controls it talks about; shown once by itself after signing in and again from Settings' Show the tour. Title of the step about selecting photos in Images.

app.tour.settings.footer.text: A short tour of how to search, sort and share your photos and files, post to Social and add friends.
app.tour.settings.footer.note: Under the Show the tour button (app.tour.show) in Settings: what the tour covers. Social is the feed section (app.shell.section_social).

app.tour.settings.title.note: Heading of the section of Settings with the button that shows the app's tour again (app.tour.show).

app.tour.show.note: Button in Settings, in the section app.tour.settings.title: shows the app's first-run tour again from its first step. Quoted in app.tour.alerts.text.

app.tour.skip.note: The first-run tour: a card over the dimmed app, one step at a time, each with a small moving drawing of the controls it talks about; shown once by itself after signing in and again from Settings' Show the tour. Button at the top right of the card that ends the tour at once (it can be shown again from Settings).

app.tour.social.text.text: Your posts and your friends' show here, newest first. Tap the heart to like one, write under it to comment, and tap the number of likes to see who liked it.
app.tour.social.text.note: The first-run tour: a card over the dimmed app, one step at a time, each with a small moving drawing of the controls it talks about; shown once by itself after signing in and again from Settings' Show the tour. Text of the step about the Social feed: the posts of the user and of their friends. The heart under a post likes it; the field under it adds a comment; the line with the number of likes opens the list of who liked it.

app.tour.social.title.note: The first-run tour: a card over the dimmed app, one step at a time, each with a small moving drawing of the controls it talks about; shown once by itself after signing in and again from Settings' Show the tour. Title of the step about the Social feed.

app.tour.upload.text.text: {upload} adds files from this phone to the open folder; select some with their circles to {share} a link or {download} them. The lock beside a folder makes it upload only: nothing in it can be deleted and old versions are kept.
app.tour.upload.text.note: The first-run tour: a card over the dimmed app, one step at a time, each with a small moving drawing of the controls it talks about; shown once by itself after signing in and again from Settings' Show the tour. Text of the step about uploading and sharing in Files. {upload}, {share} and {download} are buttons of the bar at the bottom of Files (common.upload, common.share, common.download), in bold: Upload picks files on this phone, Share sends a link to download the selected files, Download downloads them. Every file has a circle that selects it. The lock beside a folder makes it upload only: nothing in it can be deleted, and a file uploaded again under the same name keeps the one before as an older version.

app.tour.upload.title.note: The first-run tour: a card over the dimmed app, one step at a time, each with a small moving drawing of the controls it talks about; shown once by itself after signing in and again from Settings' Show the tour. Title of the second step about Files: uploading, sharing and upload-only folders.

app.tour.users.bridge.text: Keep {bridge} on to give them their own address.
app.tour.users.bridge.note: The first-run tour: a card over the dimmed app, one step at a time, each with a small moving drawing of the controls it talks about; shown once by itself after signing in and again from Settings' Show the tour. Second sentence of the step about adding users (after app.tour.users.text), as the web's web.tour.users.bridge. {bridge} is the switch under the name field in Settings › Users (app.settings.users.request_bridge), in bold; it is on from the start. On, the new user gets an address of their own on the bridge, for using the device from anywhere and for friends.

app.tour.users.text.text: Give each person their own Off The Cloud on this same device: their own photos, files and private feed, separate from yours. In {settings} › {users}, type a username, tap {add} and set their first password.
app.tour.users.text.note: The first-run tour: a card over the dimmed app, one step at a time, each with a small moving drawing of the controls it talks about; shown once by itself after signing in and again from Settings' Show the tour. Text of the step about Settings › Users, shown only to the device's owner, as the web's web.tour.users.text: each user is a separate account on the same device, with photos, files, posts and friends of their own. {settings} is the Settings section's name (app.shell.section_settings) and {users} the heading of its section (app.settings.users.title), in bold with the › between them (keep it); {add} is the button beside the field for the new user's name (common.add), in bold. The username takes lower-case letters, digits and hyphens; Add then asks for the new user's first password, which the owner gives them to sign in with. app.tour.users.bridge follows it.

app.tour.users.title.note: The first-run tour: a card over the dimmed app, one step at a time, each with a small moving drawing of the controls it talks about; shown once by itself after signing in and again from Settings' Show the tour. Title of the step about Settings › Users, shown only to the device's owner (the first account, who alone can add others): each person at home can have a user of their own on the same device.

app.tour.viewer.text.text: Tap a photo to open it, then swipe to go through them. The {info} button (ⓘ) shows when and where it was taken, the camera and a map.
app.tour.viewer.text.note: The first-run tour: a card over the dimmed app, one step at a time, each with a small moving drawing of the controls it talks about; shown once by itself after signing in and again from Settings' Show the tour. Text of the step about the full-screen viewer: a swipe goes to the next or previous photo. {info} is the name of the viewer's round i button at the top (app.photos.viewer.more_info), in bold; it shows the date taken, the place, the camera and, for photos with a location, a map. Keep the ⓘ.

app.tour.viewer.title.note: The first-run tour: a card over the dimmed app, one step at a time, each with a small moving drawing of the controls it talks about; shown once by itself after signing in and again from Settings' Show the tour. Title of the step about the full-screen photo viewer.

app.tour.welcome.text.text: This takes a minute and shows how to find, sort and share what's on your device. Every part of the app is in the bar at the bottom.
app.tour.welcome.text.note: The first-run tour: a card over the dimmed app, one step at a time, each with a small moving drawing of the controls it talks about; shown once by itself after signing in and again from Settings' Show the tour. Text of the first step on a phone held upright, where the sections are the tabs of the bar at the bottom of the screen (Alerts, Social, Files, Images, Settings); its drawing goes through them. The device is the Off The Cloud box at home that keeps everything.

app.tour.welcome.text_wide.text: This takes a minute and shows how to find, sort and share what's on your device. Every part of the app is in the menu on the left.
app.tour.welcome.text_wide.note: The first-run tour: a card over the dimmed app, one step at a time, each with a small moving drawing of the controls it talks about; shown once by itself after signing in and again from Settings' Show the tour. As app.tour.welcome.text, on a wide screen (a phone on its side, a tablet), where the sections are the items of the menu at the left of the screen.

app.tour.welcome.title.note: The first-run tour: a card over the dimmed app, one step at a time, each with a small moving drawing of the controls it talks about; shown once by itself after signing in and again from Settings' Show the tour. Title of the first step.
